prediction:
THOUGHT: This patient has an 11-year history of a chronic, productive, purulent cough with copious thick yellow-green sputum, worse in the morning, and frequent antibiotic-treated bouts of “bronchitis.” She is a non-smoker, has focal crackles and wheeze over the right middle lobe, chest x-ray showing irregular opacities in the right middle lobe with diffuse airway thickening, and sputum cultures showing heavy growth of bacteria. These features point toward a chronic suppurative airway disease rather than primary COPD or simple chronic bronchitis from smoking. The recurrent infections, large volumes of purulent sputum, focal radiographic abnormality in the right middle lobe, and diffuse bronchial wall thickening are most consistent with bronchiectasis (likely right middle lobe–predominant). Pulmonary function testing with reduced FEV1 and FVC with a preserved ratio can occur in bronchiectasis (mixed or restrictive changes from scarring/atelectasis) and does not exclude it. Chronic bronchitis could cause productive cough but is less likely in a lifelong non-smoker with focal radiographic changes and recurrent isolated lobe involvement. Definitive confirmation would be with high-resolution CT demonstrating bronchial dilation and lack of tapering, but the clinical picture and available imaging/culture data make bronchiectasis the most likely diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS: Bronchiectasis (right middle lobe–predominant)
